items.title: 68356_Howard R. Scott oral history interview
items.q: I stayed with Duke and we made records and records and records.

ctx.x: It must have been told around that he was going to change and get Joe Smith. Well, he called me, and he says, Scottie, you're open, aren't you? Well, I was open. That's what the musicians say: Are you open, and if you're open, you're open for work. You're not playing. I said, yes, Duke. He said, well, I heard you're not working with Fletcher. He says, I'd like to have you come work with me.

I didn't have the chance to feel any remorse or anything, because I went right out of the pan into the fire, so to speak. I went with him like that, the next night in the Kentucky Club. He only had one trumpet, Bubba Marley. And he had about eight pieces there, with me.
